input.question: How do new species arise?
input.ground_truth: Evolution is the very gradual change in genes over time. It isn't that one day an organism gave birth to a human. Rather, it's that over a several thousand year span, creatures stopped being a human ancestor and were instead human. There is no absolute point.

Question: How do new species arise?

Okay! Imagine you have a bunch of puppies in a big yard. Some puppies look a little different from the others—maybe one has really long fur, and another has a different color.

Now, when those puppies grow up and have their own puppies, the ones that look a little different can have puppies that look even more different. Over a *very* long time, if those special puppies keep having babies that look like them, they start to become their own kind of dog—so different that they’re like a brand new type of dog that nobody has ever seen before!

That’s how new kinds of animals—or “species”—can happen. Little changes add up over a long time, and soon you have something new!
